{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham consistently shows the worst performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (27.3%), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation yields the highest or near-highest performance: second-highest Success (78.0%), lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), highest Average Speed (12.83), and highest AD (0.399)",
    "Bright Visual Only achieves the highest Success rate (78.5%) with competitive Time-to-Target (2.61s) and Path Efficiency (0.504)",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only perform intermediately, with similar Success rates (~68-69%), but Dim Visual Only shows longer Time-to-Target (3.14s vs 3.05s) and lower Path Efficiency (0.434 vs 0.432) than ICMS Only",
    "AD follows a clear hierarchy: Combined (0.399) > Bright Visual Only (0.387) > ICMS Only (0.354) > Dim Visual Only (0.336) > Sham (0.236), suggesting angular dispersion scales with multisensory integration",
    "Average Speed is highest for Combined (12.83), followed by Bright Visual Only (12.68), with Sham showing substantially lower speed (10.74)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate shows the largest absolute difference between Sham (27.3%) and Combined/Bright Visual Only (~78-79%), representing a nearly 3-fold improvement with stimulation",
    "Time-to-Target differs dramatically: Sham (4.68s) is 83% longer than Combined (2.56s) and 79% longer than Bright Visual Only (2.61s)",
    "AD shows the most consistent gradient across paradigms, with Combined stimulation producing 69% higher angular dispersion than Sham (0.399 vs 0.236)",
    "Path Efficiency reveals substantial impairment in Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502), a 63% relative difference",
    "The gap between single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and Combined stimulation is modest for most metrics, with Combined showing marginal advantages in speed and AD"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Multisensory stimulation (Combined) and unimodal visual stimulation (Bright Visual Only) profoundly enhance mouse navigation performance compared to no stimulation (Sham), with improvements in success rate, speed, path efficiency, and angular dispersion. The particularly low performance under Sham conditions confirms that sensory feedback—whether tactile (ICMS) or visual—is essential for effective navigation. Notably, Bright Visual Only matches or exceeds Combined stimulation on success rate, suggesting that visual cues may be the dominant modality for this task. The elevated AD under stimulation conditions likely reflects more exploratory or oriented movement patterns when sensory information is available. The intermediate performance of Dim Visual Only compared to Bright Visual Only indicates luminance-dependent visual modulation. For neural prosthetic design, these results suggest that either intact visual input or ICMS can substantially improve functional outcomes, though combining both modalities offers modest additional benefits in movement dynamics (speed and angular dispersion).",
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset is heavily unbalanced across paradigms: Combined comprises 63.7% of observations (n=48,846) while Sham represents only 4.6% (n=3,505), potentially biasing population-level estimates",
    "No inferential statistics (confidence intervals, p-values, effect sizes) are provided; all comparisons are descriptive and effect magnitudes are uncertain",
    "Individual mouse effects are confounded with stimulation paradigm—different mice may have different baseline capabilities and may not experience all paradigms equally",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' is assumed from prompt instruction but its precise biomechanical meaning is unspecified in the artifacts",
    "Success is binary but analyzed as mean proportion without consideration of trial-level correlation structure or learning effects over time",
    "Extreme outliers exist in the data (e.g., Time-to-Target max=201.4s, Path Efficiency max=29.8) suggesting possible data quality issues or failed trials that may affect means",
    "Temperature=1.0 in the LLM generation parameters suggests this analysis itself may be from a stochastic generation process, though the data artifacts appear fixed"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression analysis with mouse as a random effect to estimate stimulation paradigm effects while accounting for individual differences, including calculation of confidence intervals and pairwise comparisons with multiple testing correction. Additionally, examine trial-level data for time-series effects (learning/fatigue), model Success with appropriate logistic regression, and investigate outlier handling to assess robustness of findings. Visualization of distributions (violin or box plots) would clarify whether mean differences reflect systematic shifts or are driven by outliers."
}
